warnings: Vitamin B12 is found naturally only in foods from animals (milk, curd, paneer, eggs, fish, meat); vegans need fortified foods or a supplement, and should ask a doctor what is right for them.
Pins and needles, numbness, balance problems or memory changes can be signs of low B12 and need a doctor's check soon, because some nerve damage may not fully reverse.
Long-term metformin and acid-reducing medicines (PPIs, H2 blockers) can lower B12; ask your doctor whether a B12 test is useful.
After 50, the body absorbs B12 from food less well; doctors often advise fortified foods or supplements.
No upper limit has been set for B12, but very high doses act like medicines; in kidney disease, take high-dose B-vitamin combinations only if prescribed.
High-dose folic acid can hide B12 deficiency; do not self-treat anaemia or tiredness with folic acid alone.
B12 injections are prescription treatment; the doctor decides the dose.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
